data.title: Nuvation Bio rises as Cantor initiates at overweight
data.description:
• Nuvation Bio (NUVB) is trading 2% higher Friday morning after Cantor Fitzgerald initiated the stock at overweight, saying that the Street is undervaluing its sole marketed therapy and its lead candidate.
  • The firm did not set a price target.
  • Nuvation's Ibtrozi (taletrectinib) won US FDA approval in 2025 for non-small cell lung cancer. Analyst Li Witsek said that increasing first-line use of the medicine along with multi-year duration of therapy should lead to peak sales in the US of $965M.
  • She added that safusidenib, in phase 3 for IDH1-mutant glioma (brain cancer), could have peak sales of ~$1.9B given it's been derisked by the approval of Servier's approved Voranigo (vorasidenib). 
  • "The combination of a growing commercial floor and blockbuster pipeline optionality makes NUVB a compelling, mispriced risk/reward name, in our view," Witsek wrote. "We believe there's also substantial strategic interest for a commercial-targeted oncology company like Nuvation."

data.title: Apple's next era under Ternus could place focus on AI, potentially higher investments: BofA
data.description:
With Apple (AAPL) CEO Tim Cook set to step down on Sept. 1 and be replaced by longtime executive John Ternus, Bank of America believes the next era of the tech giant could look different.

“From a cloud to an AI-enabled future, the Tim Cook era saw the concurrent growth of the public cloud that enabled the use of cloud services like Uber, Maps, etc. that merged devices with useful services,” Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan wrote in a note to clients. “We see the next era as one where devices combine AI features to become significant drivers of productivity. By combining Apple Silicon, on-device processing, privacy, operating systems, personal context, and a vast installed base, Ternus could cement Apple’s device dominance in an AI-enabled era.”

Mohan has a Buy rating and a $380 price target on Apple.

Aside from the focus on artificial intelligence, Mohan believes Apple, under Ternus, could wind up spending more money on areas that Cook places less emphasis on, including acquisitions.

“Apple has moved away from a net cash neutral objective, which in our opinion, could signal a period of higher investment in R&D, Capex, and larger M&A,” Mohan added. “The latter two have not been emphasized in the Tim Cook era, but AI could require Apple to move with a higher rate of change when the speed of innovation is accelerating with AI.”

And while Apple has gone from a company with a $360B market cap to one of more than $4T under Cook, a period of “incremental excellence may no longer be enough to redefine the company,” Mohan added.

“Ternus’s challenge will be to preserve the profitable machine Cook built while restoring a stronger sense of technological surprise,” Mohan explained.

data.title: Flowers Foods signals about $20M cost tailwind into 2027 as it accelerates innovation and new business wins
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Flowers Foods (FLO) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "As noted in our prepared remarks, our second quarter results did not meet our expectations." (CEO & Chairman of Board A. McMullian)
  • "The fresh packaged bread category remained challenging, reflecting pressure on household budgets, shifting consumer preferences and sustained competitive activity." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We're accelerating initiatives to better align our resources and value proposition with where the market is heading." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "This includes advancing innovation in smaller formats, sourdough and protein, improving our in-store execution, pursuing new business and continuing to invest behind our leading brands." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "As the Nature's Own relaunch, new business wins and innovation initiatives build momentum, we expect them to support greater stability and improved performance." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We have work to do, but we remain confident in our strategy, our brands and the actions that we are taking." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We do have some pretty significant new business wins that are coming on in the back half." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We took additional cost savings measures that will benefit the back half. And that's in addition to the roughly $200 million we've taken out of the business over the last several years." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "The speed of the shift in consumer preferences, frankly, got a little bit ahead of our innovation pipeline." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We have those things coming to fill those gaps in our offerings, whether you're thinking about protein, half loaves, sourdough, et cetera, all that's coming in the back half and then as we move into the spring of next year." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We expect some year-over-year declines in Q3, but then normalization for all the factors that Ryals mentioned related to the new business wins, reduced elasticities as we're lapping prior year pricing in Q4 and a bit of stabilization in Nature's Own from our marketing investments continue to take hold." (Chief Financial Officer Diego Scaglione)

Outlook

  • "If you look at it for the back half, a little skewed. We expect some year-over-year declines in Q3, but then normalization... in Q4." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "It's really split between our Away-from-Home business as well as our retail branded business." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "We are taking a pretty intensive review of our pricing and promotional strategy." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "The dynamics in the category are about a lot more than price." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "I would point more to consumer preference shifts." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • The transcript referenced "updated guidance" and "our current guide," but did not state numerical revenue, EPS, or full-year guidance figures; as a result, no comparison to analyst estimates is included.

Financial results

  • "I was looking at your fresh bread volume decline, which was 9.5%, and that's a big number." (Mitchell Pinheiro, Sturdivant & Co., Inc.: Question)
  • "Clearly, price had a big contributor in the price/mix." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "From -- obviously, the restructuring had some cost out in COGS. We've had good productivity as it relates to the in bakery network." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "But clearly, that's our highest fixed cost... that becomes harder and harder with the volume declines." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "Most of our commodities for the balance of this year are fully hedged." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "We had some exposure... in oil and diesel and indirectly in resin, and that's primarily in our packaging area." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)

Q&A

  • Stephen Robert Powers, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: Asked what drives back-half improvement implied by updated guidance and which initiatives matter most; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian: "3 primary factors" were "new business wins," "additional cost savings measures," and innovation filling gaps in "protein, half loaves, sourdough," with CFO Scaglione adding, "We expect some year-over-year declines in Q3" and "normalization" in Q4 as pricing is lapped and Nature's Own stabilizes.
  • Stephen Robert Powers, Deutsche Bank AG, Research Division: Asked where improvement shows up and for Nature's Own relaunch color; CFO Scaglione: "it's really split between our Away-from-Home business as well as our retail branded business" and "balanced wins across the portfolio," while CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian said, "it's going well" but "it's a little bit too early to see the actual results read through."
  • Scott Marks, Jefferies LLC, Research Division: Asked about competitive pricing/promotions and potential actions; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian: "we're taking a pretty intensive review of our pricing and promotional strategy" and argued performance is more tied to "gaps in our portfolio" such as "half loaves, sourdough, protein fiber" than price alone.
  • Scott Marks, Jefferies LLC, Research Division: Asked about inflation assumptions for 2027; CFO Scaglione: "we're still in the middle of our planning process for fiscal '27" and "I can't provide further color," but said "overall inflation has gone up" and "more to come."
  • James Salera, Stephens Inc., Research Division: Asked how Flowers offsets possible commodity inflation if pricing flexibility is lower; CFO Scaglione: "productivity measures" and "price pack architecture" are key, and "we took action coming out of Q1" creating "roughly around the $20 million tailwind we'll have going into 2027."
  • James Salera, Stephens Inc., Research Division: Asked about Dave's Killer Bread marketing pullback; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian: "it's temporary" and "we should see more normalized levels of promo and marketing spend with DKB for the balance of the year."
  • Mitchell Pinheiro, Sturdivant & Co., Inc., Research Division: Asked how gross margin held despite volume declines and about fixed-cost leverage; CFO Scaglione: "price was definitely the contributing factor" and said productivity helped but "that becomes harder and harder with the volume declines," with network optimization "more complicated and takes much longer to execute."
  • Mitchell Pinheiro, Sturdivant & Co., Inc., Research Division: Asked if Q3 volume declines moderate; CFO Scaglione: "we don't break that out" and reiterated "we expect Q3 year-on-year to be down" with "Q4" seeing "a little bit more stabilization" as wins ramp.
  • Mitchell Pinheiro, Sturdivant & Co., Inc., Research Division: Asked what consumer shifts pressured DKB; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian: "Mostly, we think that it's the growth of sourdough" and noted "that subsegment of the category has already grown to be a $1.3 billion subcategory," while adding DKB sourdough is "only" on the West Coast today.
  • Mitchell Pinheiro, Sturdivant & Co., Inc., Research Division: Asked status of the comprehensive review; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian: "we're finished with that and beginning to execute on it."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts: Slightly negative, pressing on the implied back-half acceleration, competitive pricing, and the magnitude of volume declines, including "fresh bread volume decline, which was 9.5%," and questioning whether pricing is still a lever.
  • Management: Slightly positive but candid; CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian said results "did not meet our expectations" while repeatedly emphasizing action plans and confidence, and CFO Scaglione was more cautious on 2027, saying, "I can't provide further color."
  • Versus Q1 2026 prepared remarks, Q2 tone added more explicit underperformance language ("did not meet our expectations"), while continuing to stress strategy and portfolio actions; Q1 framed execution as offsetting softness and described the comprehensive review as "gain[ing] momentum."

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • In Q2, CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian said the category was "challenging" and positioned a faster pivot to innovation in "smaller formats, sourdough and protein"; in Q1, management emphasized Better-For-You expansion, the Nature's Own relaunch, and portfolio transformation as the comprehensive review "continues to gain momentum."
  • Q2 management stated, "we're finished" with the comprehensive review and "beginning to execute on it"; Q1 described the review as ongoing and included actions such as "deprioritize 2 regional brands" (CFO Scaglione) and a dividend reset to $0.50 per share annually (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian).
  • Q2 analyst focus concentrated on near-term implied acceleration, promotional intensity, and elasticity/pricing dynamics; Q1 prepared remarks emphasized cost control, balance sheet strengthening, and brand/category performance details (including Simple Mills and Nature's Own relaunch positioning).

Risks and concerns

  • "The fresh packaged bread category remained challenging" due to "pressure on household budgets" and "sustained competitive activity." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "There has been some amount of trade down to private label and lower-priced items." (CEO & Chairman of Board McMullian)
  • "We assume that pressure in Q1" related to oil/diesel/resin exposure, and "overall inflation has gone up" as Flowers plans 2027. (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)
  • "That becomes harder and harder with the volume declines." (Chief Financial Officer Scaglione)

Final takeaway

Management said Q2 performance fell short of its expectations amid a difficult fresh packaged bread backdrop, and it is leaning on back-half new business wins, incremental cost actions, and faster innovation in smaller formats, sourdough, and protein to support stabilization. Executives described Nature's Own relaunch feedback as encouraging but early, acknowledged heightened competitive and promotional activity, and pointed to productivity and price-pack architecture as key levers as input-cost inflation trends are evaluated for 2027, including a stated roughly $20 million cost tailwind exiting 2026 into 2027.

Read the full Earnings Call Transcript

data.title: Harmony Gold sees higher full-year earnings as rising metal prices boost revenue
data.description:
Harmony Gold Mining (HMY) up 6.2% in Friday's trading after the South African miner said it expects FY 2026 earnings to rise from a year ago as 35% higher gold prices and the recent acquisition of MAC Copper helped lift revenue.

Harmony (HMY) said it expects to report earnings in the year through June 30 of $2.65-$2.85/share, up from $1.27/share a year earlier, and headline earnings of $2.45-$2.65/share.

The company said a ~$165M impairment reversal related to certain South African gold mines was recognized during the year due to significantly higher gold price assumptions applied in the valuation.

Full-year gold production of 1.43M oz was in line with company guidance, supported by strong contributions from Harmony’s (HMY) South African underground operations and the Hidden Valley mine in Papua New Guinea, underground recovered grade of 5.83 g/t was in line with guidance, and all-in sustaining costs at $2,195/oz also was within guidance.

Harmony (HMY) CEO Beyers Nel said FY 2026 was a "defining year" in the company's evolution into a diversified gold and copper producer. "We achieved gold production guidance for the 11th consecutive financial year. We also delivered on all key operating guidance metrics in full-year 2026, meeting our gold and copper production, grade, and cost targets."

data.title: China advances a step toward dissolving China Evergrande
data.description:
A Chinese court accepted on Friday a bankruptcy liquidation case against China Evergrande's (EGRNF) mainland Chinese property development subsidiary, according to media reports.

The development came a day after a court in the city of Shenzhen sentenced Hui Kan Yan, the company's founder, to life in prison for financial crimes.

A court in China's Guangzhou accepted the liquidation case of Hengda Real Estate Group,  Reuters reported.

The move suggests that the Chinese government may "have a road map" for concluding the Evergrande (EGRNF) saga, Foreky Wong, a founding partner at Fortune Ark Restructuring and a restructuring specialist, told the Associated Press.

“They will need to do these (steps) sooner or later,” he said. However, “Evergrande is such a big company. Its bankruptcy proceedings will last for a while.”

The property development giant defaulted on more than $300B of debt in 2021.

Evergrande's holding company was listed in Hong Kong, but most of its operations were in China. With the company subject to two different legal systems, it may be difficult for the Hong Kong court-appointed liquidators to claw back any assets that are recovered in China, the AP said.

data.title: Biggest stock movers Friday: ROST, MSTR, MRVL, HOOD, and more
data.description:
Stock futures edged slightly higher on Friday as markets attempted to rebound from Thursday's steep selloff. Gains were supported by a pullback in U.S. Treasury yields, though sentiment remained cautious with Brent crude hovering near $93 a barrel and lingering policy uncertainty following hawkish signals from Fed meeting minutes.

Here are some of Friday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • TG Therapeutics (TGTX) +12% - Shares jumped amid renewed takeover speculation after traders cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert suggesting the company may have attracted interest from an unnamed U.S.-listed biopharma with a $20B-$40B market capitalization.
  • Robinhood Markets (HOOD) +12% - Crypto-linked stocks rose as Bitcoin (BTC-USD) rebounded to around $77K, swinging between $72.9K and $79.4K during the day and putting it on track for its strongest weekly gain in more than two years after falling below $64K earlier this week. The rally has been fueled by falling Treasury yields, renewed optimism around U.S. crypto regulation, and a major short squeeze that liquidated roughly $2.7B in crypto short positions, lifting crypto-linked stocks including Coinbase Global (COIN) +8%, Circle Internet Group (CRCL) +6%, and Bitdeer Technologies (BTDR) +4%.
  • Strategy (MSTR) +7% - Shares rallied after the firm returned to profitability on its Bitcoin holdings, swinging to an estimated $1.4B unrealized gain as the cryptocurrency surged nearly 22% over five sessions to around $78,500. The turnaround follows a deep drawdown that saw unrealized losses top $13B when Bitcoin hit $58,000 in July.
  • Ross Stores (ROST) +3% - Shares surged after the retailer reported a stronger-than-expected quarter, with sales up 14% to $6.3B, comparable store sales up 10%, and EPS of $2.66, helped by a $253M IEEPA tariff refund. Ross raised its FY2026 EPS outlook to $8.61-$8.77 from $7.50-$7.74 and increased its planned 2026 store openings to 115.

Biggest stock losers

  • OSI Systems (OSIS) -8% - Shares plunged after Q4 revenue declined 4.1% Y/Y to $484.1M, missing estimates by $45.6M, despite non-GAAP EPS of $3.78 narrowly beating expectations. FY2027 revenue guidance of $1.875B-$1.93B came in below the $1.94B consensus, while EPS guidance of $11.13-$11.49 was broadly in line. The company also expanded its buyback authorization by 1M shares, leaving 1.08M shares available for repurchase.
  • Marvell Technology (MRVL) -6% - Shares fell despite its expanded partnership with Google ((GOOG)) to develop custom AI chips, as investors appeared to look past the deal following this week’s initial rally. Wedbush said the agreement reinforces the advantage of companies with custom-silicon design capabilities, with Marvell’s partnership spanning AI inference accelerators, storage and network controllers, and near-memory compute.
  • Flowers Foods (FLO) -5% - Shares fell after Q2 revenue declined 4% Y/Y to $1.19B, missing estimates by $40M, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.21 also came in below expectations. The company cut its FY2026 outlook, now expecting $5.07B-$5.14B in sales and $0.75-$0.85 in adjusted EPS, below the consensus of $5.17B and $0.83, respectively.

data.title: Citadel shed more than 80% of aggregate risk from Situational Awareness portfolio - CNBC
data.description:
Ken Griffin's Citadel sold more than 80% of the aggregate risk from the original Situational Awareness portfolio, the artificial-intelligence-focused hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner.

The hedge fund completed nearly 100 block trades totaling over $4 billion in market value, CNBC reported, citing a letter the hedge fund sent to investors.

"These included the largest intraday block trades of the year in 10 different names," Griffin commented in the letter. "In the United States we quickly exited the vast majority of the Vega risk, saving substantial capital in the process. Of the remaining positions in G10, only five have a gross market value greater than $250 million."

Citadel's multi-strategy fund finished up July 5.94%, bringing year-to-date performance to 12%.

Situational had reportedly held urgent talks with multiple investors about selling assets or raising fresh capital before focusing on a transaction with a single large buyer to accelerate the process and limit further losses.

Founded roughly two years ago, Situational Awareness had amassed more than $20 billion in assets under management, according to the Financial Times.

data.title: Apollo discloses 'social engineering incident' potentially impacting personal information security
data.description:
Apollo Global Management (APO) wrote to the California attorney general about a recent "social engineering incident" that may impact the security of some personal information.

The alternative asset management found in an investigation that there was unauthorized access to certain cloud platforms between July 6 and July 10. 

"During our investigation, we learned on August 12, 2026, that the information potentially impacted by this incident included your name, date of birth, contact information, home address, and your Social Security Number," said the letter to Rob Bonta.

"We have no evidence that your information has been publicly posted or used for identity theft or fraud at this time," said the letter.

"We take the confidentiality of the data entrusted to us very seriously and are therefore offering complimentary third-party identity protection and credit monitoring services," said the letter.

data.title: Nvidia, Micron among 10 stocks initiated with bullish views at BMO Capital
data.description:
BMO Capital began coverage of 12 semiconductor and quantum computing stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU), and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS).

The analysts initiated 10 stocks with an Outperform rating and two with Market Perform ratings.

"We're initiating coverage of Semiconductors and Quantum Computing with a positive outlook. We're bullish on 1) AI; and 2) Analog sectors. AI demand remains strong driven by DC infrastructure deployments and insatiable demand for AI tokens. CSP/hyperscaler and AI lab capex remain elevated in a race to reach AGI. We see AI in the early innings with many years of capex growth to support token demand (+6,050% growth) and tokenomics. We're optimistic on early-cycle recovery of analog companies. Analog upcycle is led by industrial auto is starting to pick up, while geo landscape remains positive for defense," said analysts led by Harsh Kumar.

The analysts noted that their top AI pick is Nvidia as the de facto leader with full-stack hardware/software and market share dominance. They also see Broadcom (AVGO), Micron, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Marvell Technology (MRVL), and Semtech (SMTC) well positioned in data center, or DC/AI buildouts. Analog names the analysts favor are Analog Devices (ADI), Impinj (PI), and Microchip Technology (MCHP).

Nvidia

The analysts began coverage of Nvidia with an Outperform rating and a $340 price target, noting that the stock is their top large-cap pick.

"Nvidia is our top pick as the industry's lead AI supplier. NVDA's GPU started the AI revolution and the company is now proving fully integrated AI system (NVL72) of hardware and software for compute. Demand robust for the next 12 months," said Kumar and his team.

Broadcom

Broadcom was initiated with an Outperform rating and $455 price target. The analysts noted that Broadcom is the industry leader in custom ASIC ((XPU)) and Ethernet networking. The company is working with nearly all major hyperscalers and AI labs developing XPUs, adding that visibility is strong for the next two years.

Micron

The analysts started coverage of Micron with a $1,300 price target and Outperform rating.

"Micron is a memory supplier benefiting from the AI memory supercycle. AI demand for HBM [high-bandwidth memory] continues to remain strong. Supply/demand tight leading to DRAM/NAND price increases. LTA/SCA [Long-Term Agreements/Strategic Customer Agreements] creates visibility," said the analysts.

AMD

Kumar and his team began coverage of AMD with an Outperform rating and $550 price target. AMD is second behind Nvidia in providing a complete AI system. Helios is starting to ramp up in the second half of 2026. Multi-year deals, secured with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic for Helios racks into 2030, the analysts added.

Marvell

BMO initiated coverage of Marvell with a $250 price target and an Outperform rating. The analysts noted that Marvell is a leading DC infrastructure supplier. The company is a leader in PAM4 optical connectivity. Networking portfolio supports scale up, out, and across. The company is emerging as a key supplier in XPU and XPU-attach, according to the analysts.

Semtech

Semtech was initiated with a $155 price target and an Outperform rating. "Semtech is a niche semiconductor supplier. Growth led by optical DC modules. Revenues expected to step up from LPO/ACC [Linear Pluggable Optics/Active Copper Cable] connectivity. Sustained steady 15-20% growth from LoRa," said Kumar and his team.

Analog Devices

The analysts started coverage with an Outperform rating and a $430 price target. The analysts noted that Analog Devices is a well-managed company positioned for the broader semiconductor cycle upturn. Revenues are 75% industrial/auto markets, and demand signals are improving. In addition, customer orders are increasing, and backlog is starting to grow. 

Impinj

The analysts said Impinj is the leader in RFID with an estimated 65% share of the global market. Channel inventory is cleared. Total Addressable Market, or TAM, is increasing as use cases are expanding into general merchandising in the food/meat category, the analysts added. The stock was initiated with an Outperform rating and a $220 price target.

Microchip Technology 

BMO began coverage with an Outperform rating and a $95 price target. The analysts said that Microchip benefits from improving semi-cycles and favorable macro conditions. Industrial is in full swing while auto is showing early recovery. Improved utilization rates help drive margins higher, the analysts added.

D-Wave

"In quantum computing, we initiate DWave with OP rating as we see best fit for commercial success, considering its presence in two leading quantum approaches. The quantum computing industry is still in its early days, and we see it as a long-term growth story," said Kumar and his team. The stock was initiated with an Outperform rating and a $35 price target.

Macom Technology (MTSI) and Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) were initiated with Market Perform ratings, with price targets of $355 and $70, respectively.

data.title: Walmart rolling out Tap to Pay for contactless check-out
data.description:
• Walmart (WMT) is adding a contactless payment system, including Apple Pay, at select stores and Sam’s Club locations beginning August 24, with a further expansion planned for later this year.
  • Tap to Pay at Walmart (WMT) will allow shoppers to hold a credit card, phone, or smartwatch near a card reader to send payment data instantly without swiping or inserting a credit or debit card. Customers can also add eligible Walmart, Sam’s Club, and OnePay cards to their digital wallets. 
  • While other retailers embraced Apple Pay for contactless checkout, Walmart (WMT) opted to stick with its own QR code-based system, Walmart Pay, despite consumers’ preference for Apple Pay.
  • Despite welcome news for a large contingent of Walmart shoppers, the news failed to put a dent in the negative price action for the stock following disappointing second-quarter results.
